layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video matting has broad applications, from adding in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teresting effects to casually captured movies to assisting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video production professionals. Matting with associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects such as shadows and reflections has also attracted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing research activity, and methods like Omnimatte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been proposed to separate dynamic foreground ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects of interest into their own layers. However, prior works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represent video backgrounds as 2D image layers, limiting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their capacity to express more complicated scenes, thus hin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dering application to real-world videos. In this paper, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propose a novel video matting method, OmnimatteRF, that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combines dynamic 2D foreground layers and a 3D back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground model. The 2D layers preserve the details of the sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects, while the 3D background robustly reconstructs scenes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in real-world videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that our method reconstructs scenes with better quality on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various videos.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video matting is the problem of separating a video into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple layers with associated alpha mattes such that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers are composited back to the original video. It has a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wide variety of applications in video editing as it allows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for substituting layers or processing them individually be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fore compositing back, and thus has been studied well over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decades. In typical applications like rotoscoping in video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: production and background blurring in online meetings, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: goal is to obtain the masks containing only the object of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interest. In many cases, however, it is often preferred to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be able to create video mattes that include not only the ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject of interest but also its associated effects, like shadow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and reflections. This could reduce the often-required, ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ditional manual segmentation of secondary effects and help

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase realism in the resulting edited video. Being able

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to factor out the related effects of foreground objects also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: helps reconstruct a clean background, which is preferred in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (a) Omnimatte BG

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (b) Omnimatte FG

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (c) Our BG

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (d) Our FG

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1. Video with parallax effects. Limited by their 2D im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age representation (a), previous works such as Omnimatte fail to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: handle videos with parallax effects in the background. Their fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground layer (b) has to capture (dis)occlusion effects to minimize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the reconstruction loss. In contrast, our method employs a 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background (c), enabling us to obtain clean foreground layers (d).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications like object removal. Despite these benefits, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem is much more ill-posed and has been much less ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plored than the conventional matting problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The most promising attempt to tackle this problem is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Omnimatte [21]. Omnimattes are RGBA layers that cap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture dynamic foreground objects and their associated ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects. Given a video and one or more coarse mask videos,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each corresponding to a foreground object of interest, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method reconstructs an omnimatte for each object, in addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion to a static background that is free from all of the ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects of interest and their associated effects. While Om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimatte [21] works well for many videos, it is limited by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its use of homography to model backgrounds, which re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quires the background be planar or the video contains only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rotational motion. This is not the case as long as there ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ists parallax caused by camera motions and objects occlude

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each other. This limitation hinders its application in many

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: real-world videos, as shown in Fig. 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: D2NeRF [36] attempts to address this issue using two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: radiance fields, which model the dynamic and static part of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the scene. The method works entirely in 3D and can han-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dle complicated scenes with significant camera motion. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is also self-supervised in the sense that no mask input is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: necessary. However, it separates all moving objects from a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: static background and it is not clear how to incorporate 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guidance defined on video such as rough masks. Further, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot independently model multiple foreground objects. A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simple solution of modeling each foreground object with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separate radiance field could lead to excessive training time,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet it is not clear how motions could be separated meaning-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully in each radiance field.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose a method that has the benefit of both by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combining 2D foreground layers with a 3D background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model. The lightweight 2D foreground layers can repre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sent multiple object layers, including complicated objects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motions, and effects that may be challenging to be mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eled in 3D. At the same time, modeling background in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D enables handling background of complex geometry and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-rotational camera motions, allowing for processing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: broader set of videos than 2D methods. We call this method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OmnimatteRF and show in experiments that it works ro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bustly on various videos without per-video parameter tun-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing. To quantitatively evaluate the background separation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a 3D scene, D²NeRF released a dataset of 5 videos ren-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dered with Kubrics, which are simple indoor scenes with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few pieces of furniture and some moving objects that cast

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solid shadows. We also render five videos from open-source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Blender movies [6] with sophisticated motions and lighting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions for more realistic and challenging settings. Our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method outperforms prior works in both datasets, and we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: release the videos to facilitate future research.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, our contributions include the following:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. We propose a novel method to make Omnimatte [21]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more robust by better modeling the static background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 3D using radiance fields [22].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Utilizing the omnimatte masks, we propose a simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet effective re-training step to obtain a clean static 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruction from videos with moving subjects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. We release a new dataset of 5 challenging video se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quences rendered from open-source blender movies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [6] with ground truths to better facilitate the develop-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment and evaluation of the video matting with associ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ated effects (aka omnimatting [21]) problem.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Matting. There is a long line of work exploring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video matting due to its importance in video editing. Green

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screening and rotoscoping are critical first steps in any vi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sual effects pipeline. The matting problem aims to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the foreground subjects into their own RGBA layers and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: separate them from the background RGB layer, which is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highly under-constrained problem. Many approaches have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utilized motion and depth cues in addition to integrating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: user interactions [7, 3, 32, 16, 9]. Background Video Mat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting [18] specifically addresses real-time video matting of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: people and preserving strand-level hair details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Matting with Associated Effects. Video matting is often

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: insufficient, as foreground subjects might have associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects like shadows or reflections that need to be extracted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the foreground RGBA layers. This problem has not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been explored as extensively and, in practice, is often dealt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with manually using advanced interactive rotoscoping tools

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [15]. Omnimatte [21] was the first to propose a generic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework capable of learning any associated effect. Pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vious works often specifically addressed associated effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like shadows [34, 33]. The ability to obtain matte layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with associated effects has many exciting applications, such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as re-timing motions of different people [20], consistent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background editing [13, 14], background subtraction, green

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: screening, and many other video effects [21]. Recently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FactorMatte [12] has been proposed to improve the qual-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity with data augmentation and conditional priors. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works have in common that they take predefined masks that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hint at the foreground objects and decompose each video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into several layers, with one object in each layer with its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated effects. Then, there is a background layer, a 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: static image, or a deformable atlas shared by all the frames.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The background is warped and cropped via a homography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to render each frame. While the foreground layers have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown great potential in capturing dynamics, their single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image background limits the application of these methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to videos with planar environments without parallax effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: caused by camera motion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Radiance Fields. Radiance fields (RF) emerged as 3D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representations capable of capturing geometric details and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: photorealistic appearances [22]. Radiance fields model the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D scene as a continuous function that maps the position

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the viewing direction of any point in world space to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its color and opacity. Novel views can be synthesized via

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volume rendering along rays cast. This continuous func-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion is learned by optimizing with a reconstruction loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the rendered images. This view-dependent volumetric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representation can model various challenging scenes that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous surface-based methods struggled to handle: e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shiny surfaces like metals or fuzzy surfaces like hair or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fur. Since then, it has been extended along multiple axes:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better appearance modeling (e.g., reflection and refraction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [31, 5, 2, 1], faster optimization [8, 27, 23] and model-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing dynamic scenes [38, 17, 10, 19]. Since the MLP-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based implicit RF representations are slow to train, we use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: voxel-based explicit radiance field representations [8] [27]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specifically, we use the factorized voxel grid representation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from [8].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Self-Supervised Video Dynamics Factoring. Another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: related work is video dynamics factoring without needing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a predefined mask. One recent work is deformable sprites

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [39] that rely only on motion cues. Similar to other video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matting works, it has a 2D foreground and background lay-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers and the same limitations as Omnimatte. For modeling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 3D,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 36] proposes to decouple the scene with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two radiance fields, one for the dynamic content and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other for the statics. D2NeRF[36] handles a special case of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matting with only one foreground object, and, compared to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the other methods, it is not limited to planar backgrounds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, the self-supervised method relies on the heuristics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that require per-video hyper-parameter tuning and does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robustly generalize to new videos. The quality of the fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground reconstruction can also be limited for objects that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have large nonrigid motions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We, therefore, propose a method for video matting with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated effects that has the advantages of supervised 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mattes that support multiple individual objects with great

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: details, as well as 3D background decoupling that works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with non-planar videos.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The concept of omnimattes is proposed by Lu et al. [21],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extending RGBA video mattes to capture associated effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the objects of interest like shadows and reflections. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: avoid any confusion, in the following text, we refer to their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work as capital Omnimatte, and the resulting RGBA layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as italic omnimatte. In the matting setup, the user prepares

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a video of T frames

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , and N ordered mask layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , each containing a coarse mask video of an object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of interest. The video's camera parameters are also precom-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: puted as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The goal is to predict RGBA foreground layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that contain the objects together with their associated ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects, and a background layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is clean and free

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the effects cast by the foreground objects. An input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should be reconstructed by alpha compositing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground layers above the background.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In Omnimatte, the background is represented by a static

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D image and a homography transform

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . To compose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a frame, part of the static background is extracted accord-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing to the estimated homography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The key idea of our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work is to represent the static background in 3D using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: radiance field, while keeping the foreground in 2D to bet-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ter capture the dynamics of objects. We employ an explicit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factorized voxel-based radiance field [8] to model the back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground. In this case,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represents a camera pose, and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background frame is rendered with volume rendering. Note

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the foreground layers are still 2D videos. We refer to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this combination as the OmnimatteRF model.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. The OmnimatteRF Model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An outline of our model is depicted in Figure 2. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model has two independent branches: foreground and back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground. For any given frame, the foreground branch pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dicts an RGBA image (omnimatte) for each object, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background branch renders a single RGB image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Preprocessing. Following similar works, we use an off-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the-shelf model RAFT [29] to predict optical flow between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neighboring frames. The flow is used as an auxiliary input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and ground truth for supervision, denoted by

layout_dets.text: 3.3. Clean Background via Masked Retraining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When the pipeline is trained jointly as described above,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it is sometimes observed that the background radiance field

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 3(c)). Compared to 2D images, 3D radiance fields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are so much more capable that they can exploit distorted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geometry constructs, such as holes and floaters, to capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time information. For example, as the camera moves over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time, there may be a correlation between whether a surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is covered by shadow and the direction the surface is viewed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We illustrate this problem in Fig. 3 and explain the cause

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at an intuitive level. The foreground branch is bootstrapped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to produce alpha values that match the coarse mask inputs,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which include only the object without the associated effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In other words,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values are close to one at the object, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zero in the shadows (for simplicity, we consider one fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground layer in which the object casts a shadow, like in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 3). At a pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The reconstruction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss will therefore encourage

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to match the color of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the shadow for a ray shot toward this location.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As training proceeds,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will then gradually increase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the predicted alpha values at the shadowed regions. If the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to no constraint to the background color at the pixel. As a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is unable to learn to remove the shadow color that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it produces for the ray towards frame

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There are also cases where the shadow is soft and α is in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between. In these cases, the problem remains ambiguous.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Therefore, we propose to obtain clean background re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: construction via an optional optimization step. In joint

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training, the foreground omnimatte layers can capture most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated effects, including the parts with leaked content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the background layer. The alpha layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples from the foreground region where alpha values are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three Blender movies in Blender Studio [6]. Compared to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kubri cs, they feature more complicated scenes and light-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing conditions, large nonrigid motion of the characters, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher resolution. To ensure usability, we manually edit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the camera trajectories so that there are sufficient camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motions and the actors have reasonable sizes. We render

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the clips with and without the actors to obtain input and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground truth for background reconstruction evaluation pur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poses. The camera poses are also exported.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2. Experiment Setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate the performance of our proposed method on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: four datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Movies: our novel challenging dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Kubrics: the dataset generated and used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which consists of five scenes of moving objects from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D Warehouse [30] rendered with Kubric [11].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. DAVIS [24, 25]: short clips with moving foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subjects, like humans, cars, and animals. This dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is widely used to evaluate 2D-background matting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. Wi 1d: in-the-wild sequences collected from the inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: net that are closer to casually captured videos, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural and noisier camera motions, including trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lations and rotations, as well as objects at different dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tances from the camera. Naturally, these videos have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backgrounds that are challenging for pure 2D methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kubrics and Movies are synthetic datasets with clean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background layer renderings available. Note that novel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: view synthesis is not the focus of our method, so we eval-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uate the background with input views. Both datasets have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known camera poses and object masks which are used for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training and evaluation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DAVIS and Wild are real-world videos without clean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background. Therefore, we only perform a qualitative eval-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uation to demonstrate the robustness of our method. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos in Wild we recover camera poses with COLMAP.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For videos that COLMAP cannot process reliably, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DAVIS videos, we use poses from RoDynRF [19].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 4. Background Reconstruction. We show examples of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results presented in quantitative evaluations. For videos with par-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allax effects, 3D methods like D²NeRF and ours reconstruct less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distorted background than Omnimatte and LNA.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To obtain coarse object masks, we attempt to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them with pre-trained object segmentation models from De-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tectron 2 [37]. In case it does not work, we use the Roto

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Brush tool in Adobe After Effects. Detailed procedures are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described in the supplementary material. It takes about 10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minutes of manual effort to produce a 200-frame mask.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For all videos, we also estimate homographies with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LoFTR [28] and OpenCV to enable Omnimatte processing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As mentioned in D2NeRF [36], the method is sensitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to hyperparameters. The authors released five sets of con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: figurations for different videos. We experiment with every

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video using all provided configurations and report the best-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performing ones.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3. Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our network is built upon the publicly available offi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cial implementation of Omnimatte [21], and TensoRF [8].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The videos in Kubrics have resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all methods run at the resolution 256 × 256. For videos in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other datasets with a higher resolution of 1920 × 1080, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downsample them by a factor of 4.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We optimize the networks for up to 15,000 steps. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is set to 0.001 and is exponentially de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cayed after 10,000 steps. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we use the learning rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scheduling scheme of TensoRF. Training takes up to 6 hours

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a single RTX3090 GPU. Detailed network architecture,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hyper-parameters and timing data are presented in the sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plementary. Our code and datasets will also be made pub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: licly available.

layout_dets.text: 4.6. Ablation Studies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.6.1 Loss Terms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present background reconstruction results without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 6. For video sequences with rotational camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poses, the model struggles to extract 3D information from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input videos because of a lack of 3D clues. This loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is critical to extending our method to a broader range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos. The effects of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are also demonstrated in Fig. 6.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The auxiliary task improves foreground quality and reduces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unrelated content.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.6.2 Clean Background Retraining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We employ an additional step for real-world sequences to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimize a clean background from scratch. In Fig. 7, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compare the background layer from the initial joint opti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mization and the final result. This is a simple yet robust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: way to obtain a better background.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.7. Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We list some limitations that future works can explore.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. If a background region is covered by shadows nearly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all of the time, the background model cannot recover

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its color correctly. An example from a Movies video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is shown in Fig. 8. In theory, an omnimatte layer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has an alpha channel and can capture only the addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive shadow that allows the background to have the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: original color. However, this problem is largely under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constrained in the current setting, making it ambiguous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and leading the background to unsatisfying solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. The foreground layer captures irrelevant content. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: real-world videos, unrelated motions often exist in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the background, like swaying trees and moving cars.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These effects cannot be modeled by the static radiance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: field and will be captured by the foreground layer re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gardless of their association with the object. Possible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directions include i) using a dummy 2D layer to catch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such content or ii) a deformable 3D background model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with additional regularization to address the ambiguity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as both background and foreground can model motion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Foreground objects may have missing parts in the omn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imatte layers if they're occluded. Since our foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network predicts pixel values for alpha composition, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: does not always hallucinate the occluded parts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. The video resolution is limited. This is primarily due

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the U-Net architecture of the foreground model in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: herited from Omnimatte. Higher resolutions can po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentially be supported with the use of other lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image encoders.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. The foreground layer may capture different content

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when the weights are randomly initialized differently.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We include visual results in the supplementary materi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: als.
